instructions: Rowkery gives read-only access to the database connections the user shared from the Rowkery app. Start with list_connections. Before writing a query, look at the tables with list_tables or search_schema and call describe_table for each table you will use, so you know its columns and indexes. Filter on indexed columns, aggregate in SQL (count, sum, group by) instead of pulling rows, and ask for no more rows than you will read. Queries are single SELECT statements; results are capped (200 rows by default, 1000 at most) and a plan that reads a table of more than 100,000 rows end to end is refused, so rewrite it with an indexed WHERE. explain shows the plan without running the query. Columns the user marked sensitive come back masked (masked: and ten hex digits; the same value always gives the same stand-in). You can return or count a masked column (on SQLite only return it) but not filter, sort, group or join on it; describe_table lists them. For a slow or stuck database, sessions shows what's running, what each session waits on and who blocks whom. Queries never change data: the session is read-only. To change data, call propose_change with the INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE statements and why: the user reviews a dry run in Rowkery and commits or rejects it, and check_proposal tells you which. Don't send a rejected change again. describe_table gives what a change needs (columns, defaults, keys, enum labels), so don't query existing rows to copy their style or values. Read only the rows a change depends on, such as the one row it updates, and select only the columns you need.

tools.description: What's running on a Postgres database: each session's user, application, state, how long it has been at it, what it waits on and which sessions block it. Blockers come first; idle sessions are left out unless include_idle. Query text has its values replaced by ?, and a query on a table not shared with you is blanked.

tools.name: sessions

tools.description: Ask the user to make a change to the data. Send INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements (no CTEs, RETURNING, UPDATE … FROM or DELETE … USING) on shared tables, with reason saying why. Nothing runs now: Rowkery shows the user a dry run and only they can commit it. Returns an id at once; call check_proposal later to learn whether it was committed, rejected or expired (after 24 h). Masked columns can't be mentioned, and functions defined in the database can't be called.
